title: 题乌江亭
author: 杜牧
intro: At the river where the great warlord Xiang Yu took his own life rather than retreat, Du Mu argues with history: a real hero swallows his shame and tries again. The poem gave Chinese the idiom 卷土重来, “to come back with a whirl of dust”.
analysis: 公元前202年，楚霸王项羽被刘邦打败，逃到乌江边。乌江亭长劝他渡江回江东（今天的江浙一带）重新开始，他却说当年带八千江东子弟出来，如今没有一人回去，没脸再见江东父老，于是自杀。一千年后，杜牧经过乌江亭，写下这首诗，对这件事发表不同的看法：打仗胜败是兵家常事，谁也料不到；能忍受羞辱、不怕失败，才是真正的男子汉。江东人才那么多，如果他回去，说不定还能“卷土重来”——重新带着人马杀回来。古人写历史人物多是感叹或赞美，杜牧却提出“如果当时……”的假设，这种写法叫“翻案”，意思是推翻常见的看法。“卷土重来”后来成了常用成语，指失败后重新恢复力量。
analysisEn: In 202 BC Xiang Yu, the mighty “Hegemon-King of Chu”, was crushed by Liu Bang, the future founder of the Han dynasty, and fled to the Wujiang River. The local official offered him a boat home to Jiangdong, the lands east of the Yangtze where he had first raised his army. Xiang Yu refused. He had led eight thousand young men of Jiangdong into war, and not one was coming back with him; how could he face their fathers? He took his own life on the riverbank. A thousand years later Du Mu passed the pavilion there and disagreed. Winning and losing, he says, are part of every soldier’s life — no one can predict them. Swallowing shame and enduring defeat is what makes a real man. Jiangdong had plenty of talented young men; had Xiang Yu gone home, who knows whether he might have come back again, raising a whirl of dust. Most poets wrote about historical heroes to praise or mourn them; Du Mu instead asks “what if?” and overturns the usual verdict. The phrase 卷土重来, “to roll up the dust and come again”, became a common idiom for making a comeback after failure.
background: Du Mu (803–c. 852) was a late-Tang official and poet, famous for short, sharp poems about history. He is said to have written this when he passed the Wujiang pavilion (in today’s Anhui) while travelling as an official in the south.
pronunciation: 卷土 juǎn tǔ；重来 chóng lái（不读 zhòng）；不期 bù qī。
version: 采用通行版本。第三句有的版本作“江东子弟多豪俊”，网站用“多才俊”。

lines.py: shèng bài bīng jiā shì bù qī
lines.lit: Victory and defeat are a soldier’s business, not to be foreseen;
lines.en: No general can know in advance if he will win or lose;

lines.py: bāo xiū rěn chǐ shì nán ér
lines.lit: to bear shame and endure disgrace — that is a man.
lines.en: the one who can swallow his shame is the real man.

lines.py: jiāng dōng zǐ dì duō cái jùn
lines.lit: The young men east of the river had many talents;
lines.en: East of the river there were still plenty of brave young men —

lines.py: juǎn tǔ chóng lái wèi kě zhī
lines.lit: rolling up the dust and coming again — that cannot be known.
lines.en: who can say he would not have stormed back in a cloud of dust?

words.en: the Wujiang River (in today’s Anhui), where Xiang Yu died
military men; those who wage war
words.note: 今天还说“胜败乃兵家常事”，意思是成败很正常。
古义“不能预料”；今天“不期而遇”是“没有约好却碰见”。

words.en: to swallow shame and bear disgrace
words.note: 今天常说“忍辱负重”，意思相近。

words.en: east of the Yangtze — Xiang Yu’s home region
words.note: 指长江下游南岸一带，今天的江苏南部、浙江一带。
今天还有“子弟兵”“八旗子弟”。
书面语，今天有“青年才俊”。

words.en: to make a comeback (lit. roll up the dust and come again)
words.note: 出自这首诗，今天是常用成语，指失败后重新恢复力量再来。

words.en: cannot be known; who can tell
words.note: 现代汉语说“说不定”“不一定”。

imagery.name: 江
imagery.zh: 乌江是项羽人生的终点，江对岸的江东却是他重新开始的希望；一条江，隔开了绝望和“卷土重来”的可能。
imagery.en: The Wujiang River is where Xiang Yu’s story ended, yet across it lay Jiangdong and a second chance; the river divides despair from the comeback he never tried.
